title: A 1000-hour EEG-EMG-audio dataset of Japanese speech production
authors: Motoshige Sato; Ilya Horiguchi; Masakazu Inoue; Kenichi Tomeoka; Eri Hatakeyama; Yuya Kita; Atsushi Yamamoto; Ippei Fujisawa; Shuntaro Sasai
summary: A 1020-hour EEG-EMG-audio dataset of Japanese overt speech from three participants, with signal-quality and physiological validation but no decoding benchmarks.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Only three Japanese male participants; evaluation limited to signal-quality checks without downstream decoding experiments.

title: A First Exploration of Neuromorphic OT-CFM for Multi-Speaker VSR
authors: Lin Chen; Jingping Fang; Hairui Liu; Chenyang Xu; Junhao Chen; Xiaorui Li; Weidong Cai; Xiaoming Chen
summary: Neuromorphic OT-CFM (LipsFlow) for multi-speaker visual speech recognition from event streams; 22.3% WER and 19.8% VER on DVS-Lip with 240 ms latency.
sensor: Event streams from RGB video or DVS dataset (camera)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 22.3% WER, 19.8% VER on DVS-Lip, 240 ms latency
limitations: Camera-based, not a wearable SSI; author-reported benchmark results only; vocabulary and speaker split details limited; on-device, walking and clinical use untested.

title: AESSI: An Around-Ear Silent Speech Interface for Cross-Day Online Reuse without Test-Day Calibration
authors: Xiran Xu; Mochu Dong; Yujie Yan; Chenxi Wang; Yu Jiao; Jing Chen
summary: Around-ear cEEGrid system recognizing 25 fixed Mandarin sentences from silent articulation without test-day calibration; 92.24% mean accuracy on held-out later-day sessions and 98.00% in 250 live trials 21+ days later.
sensor: Bilateral around-ear cEEGrid electrodes (mixed EMG/EEG), 18 channels
speaker: Both
key_result: 92.24% accuracy, cross-day held-out sessions, no test-day calibration, chance 4%; 98.00% live (245/250)
limitations: Closed 25-sentence set only; mixed signal sources not separated; open-vocabulary conversation, walking, noise, long wear and patient use untested; live test used a single seed.

title: Affect Decoding in Phonated and Silent Speech Production from Surface EMG
authors: Simon Pistrosch; Kleanthis Avramidis; Zhao Ren; Tiantian Feng; Jihwan Lee; Monica Gonzalez-Machorro; Anton Batliner; Tanja Schultz; Shrikanth Narayanan; Björn W. Schuller
summary: Binary affect (polite vs frustrated) classification from facial/neck sEMG in phonated and silent speech; silent-only within-subject AUC 0.829, but transfer to unseen speakers is weak.
speaker: Both
key_result: Silent-only within-subject AUC 0.829; held-out-speaker EMG AUC 0.567-0.574
limitations: Small imbalanced cohort; facial expression and speech motor activity not separated; fixed task order; no independent-day, mobile or patient testing.

title: Articulatory movements influence electromagnetic wave transmission through the vocal tract
authors: Remi Blandin; Martin Laabs; Rudolf von Bunau; Bryn Lloyd; Silvia Farcito; Denys Nikolayev; Gabriela Hossu; Peter Birkholz; Dirk Plettemeier
summary: Physical modeling and measurement of contact RF transmission through the vocal tract for three sustained vowels in two participants; simulations qualitatively agree with measurements below about 3 GHz.
sensor: Two cheek-mounted bow-tie antennas with lab VNA; MRI models
task: Physical modeling of articulatory RF sensing
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Between-vowel transmission differences up to 15 dB near 1.5 GHz; repetition variation ~5-10 dB
limitations: Only two participants and three vowels; agreement mainly qualitative with no error metric; no recognition system, wearable device or patient use.

title: AVSRBench: A Multi-Condition AVSR Benchmark
authors: Rishabh Jain; Naomi Harte
summary: Benchmark comparing visual-only, audio-only and audio-visual speech recognition across six datasets; sub-1% AV WER on LRS3, visual-only collapses out of domain, and AV fusion helps clearly mainly under Lombard speech.
vocabulary: Dataset-dependent; continuous open vocabulary (GRID fixed grammar)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 0.79% AV WER on LRS3 (Llama-AVSR); visual-only WER 110.07% on RoomReader-AV (Auto-AVSR)
limitations: Uses fixed public checkpoints without retraining; camera-based AVSR rather than wearable SSI; no real-time or on-device measurement; limited speaker-split and statistical detail.

title: Brain-to-Speech: Prosody Feature Engineering and Transformer-Based Reconstruction
authors: Mohammed Salah Al-Radhi; Géza Németh; Andon Tchechmedjiev; Binbin Xu
summary: Transformer-based speech reconstruction from intracranial sEEG with prosody feature engineering; reports Pearson correlation 0.91, MCD 3.92 and STOI 0.73.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: PC 0.91, MCD 3.92, STOI 0.73, HNR 12.7 dB, tenfold cross-validation
limitations: Split unit and participant separation unspecified; neural prosody features not validated; no human intelligibility, WER or latency measurement.

title: Brain2Speech-Net: Intelligible, Real-Time Brain-to-Speech Synthesis Without Text Decoding
authors: Shreeram Suresh Chandra; Zexin Cai; Yu Tsao; Simon King; Berrak Sisman
summary: Text-free synthesis of attempted speech from intracortical recordings in one participant with ALS; 47.2% WER on unseen utterances versus 6.8% on a training-set sample, with faster-than-real-time throughput (RTF ~0.5).
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 47.2% WER on unseen utterances (cascades 20.6-22.9%); RTF 0.532
limitations: Single implanted participant, offline only; closed-set score is from training data; future-dependent inference prevents streaming claims; MOS study showed reference text; synthetic single-speaker voice.

title: Comparison of sEMG Encoding Accuracy Across Speech Modes Using Articulatory and Phoneme Features
authors: Chenqian Le; Ruisi Li; Beatrice Fumagalli; Yasamin Esmaeili; Xupeng Chen; Amirhossein Khalilian-Gourtani; Tianyu He; Adeen Flinker; Yao Wang
summary: Forward encoding of sEMG envelopes from articulatory (SPARC) versus phoneme features across speech modes; articulatory features predict muscle activity better on most channels in 24 participants.
task: Forward encoding of sEMG from speech features
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Gaddy replication voiced r 0.455 (SPARC) vs 0.443 (phoneme); main results plotted, not tabulated
limitations: Within-subject only; articulatory features inferred from paired voiced audio; DTW may inflate correlations; no actual decoding or synthesis gains tested.

title: Cross-Modal Masking for Robust Silent Speech Synthesis Using sEMG and Lipreading
authors: Eder del Blanco; David Gimeno-Gómez; Eva Navas; Carlos-D. Martínez-Hinarejos; Inma Hernáez
summary: Silent speech synthesis fusing sEMG and lipreading with cross-modal masked training, improving performance and robustness to modality degradation over monomodal baselines.
sensor: 8 bipolar face/neck sEMG sensors plus RGB lip video
task: Speech synthesis from sEMG and video
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Limited-vocabulary Spanish data; adaptation to laryngectomized users limited; no real-time, wearable or spontaneous-speech evaluation.

title: CS-ETS: Chaos-Inspired Samba-Based EMG-To-Speech Synthesis with Nonlinear Chaotic Losses
authors: Sajid Fardin Dipto; Tarikul Islam Tamiti; David Vergano; Luke Baja-Ricketts; Anomadarshi Barua
summary: Smaller chaos-inspired Samba-based EMG-to-speech model with nonlinear losses; WER improves modestly from 42.20% to 41.26% while parameters drop from 54.10M to 32.03M.
vocabulary: Open-vocabulary EMG corpus; size not specified
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 41.26% WER vs 42.20% baseline; 32.03M parameters
limitations: Single speaker and dataset; large acoustic-metric gains confounded by target-audio alignment applied only to the proposed output; insufficient split details and no confidence intervals.

title: Do EEG Foundation Models Transfer to Speech? A Benchmark on Overt and Imagined Speech Decoding
authors: Owais Mujtaba Khanday; Mohamed Baha Ben Ticha; Sanae Belfrouh; Marc Ouellet; Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez
summary: Benchmark of EEG foundation models versus conventional models for overt and imagined speech decoding on two datasets; general EEG pretraining shows no consistent advantage and word decoding stays near chance.
speaker: Both
key_result: Speech-mode accuracy 61.3% (EEGNet) vs 33.3% chance; 60-word accuracy 1.7-2.9% vs 1.7% chance
limitations: Test-subject-informed early stopping weakens unseen-user claims; small cohorts and fixed vocabularies; no pretraining ablation, multiple seeds or online evaluation.

title: EEG-Based Imagined Speech Decoding Using a Hybrid CNN-SNN Architecture
authors: Fatima Shalhoub; Mariam Al Mawla; Kabalan Chaccour; Iván López-Espejo; Hoda Fares
summary: Hybrid CNN-SNN classifier for five-class EEG imagined speech; reports 80.13% accuracy and 80.14% F1 in offline subject-dependent evaluation, about 98 ms GPU prediction time per trial.
vocabulary: 5 words/phrases (Hello, Help me, Stop, Thank you, Yes)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 80.13% accuracy, 5 classes, subject-dependent, validation subset
limitations: Evaluated on the validation subset, not the hidden test set; no per-subject results, uncertainty or matched CNN/SNN ablation; power and online use unmeasured.

title: EMG-to-Speech with Fewer Channels
authors: Injune Hwang; Jaejun Lee; Kyogu Lee
summary: Channel-reduction study for EMG-to-speech using exhaustive subset search and full-channel pretraining; best four-channel subsets reach about 47.2% WER versus roughly 35% with all eight channels.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 47.2% WER, best 4-channel subset (full-channel ~35%)
limitations: Single subject; subset selection not clearly independent of reporting; no repeated runs or physically built reduced-channel device.

title: iPhoneme: Brain-to-Text Communication for ALS Using ConformerXL Decoding
authors: Yoonmin Cha; Dawit Chun; Sung Park
summary: ConformerXL-based intracortical brain-to-text decoding for ALS with a proposed gaze-confirmation interface; WFST decoding reaches 7.86% phoneme error rate retrospectively in one participant.
vocabulary: 42 phoneme classes; word vocabulary not reported
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 7.86% PER with WFST (180 ms); 26.61% word error
limitations: No clearly independent final test (validation informs tuning); single participant, retrospective; noncausal model; latency incompletely measured; gaze interface not user-validated.

title: Lip-Siri: Contactless Open-Sentence Silent Speech with Wi-Fi Backscatter
authors: Ye Tian; Haohua Du; Chao Gu; Junyang Zhang; Shanyue Wang; Hao Zhou; Jiahui Hou; Xiang-Yang Li
summary: Lip-Siri senses lip motion contactlessly with Wi-Fi frequency-shifted backscatter and decodes lexicon-constrained sentences, reporting 85.61% word accuracy and 36.87% sentence WER on a random 80/20 split plus three held-out users.
sensor: Wi-Fi backscatter tag with SDR (USRP) transceivers
speaker: Both
key_result: 85.61% word accuracy, 36.87% sentence WER, random 80/20 split; new users 81.5-85.5%
limitations: Lexicon composition is not unseen-word recognition; main split is not sentence-disjoint, and SDR hardware, manual start/end clicks and 50 cm geometry limit deployment.

title: LipSody: Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Enhanced Prosody Consistency
authors: Jaejun Lee; Yoori Oh; Kyogu Lee
summary: LipSody, lip-to-speech synthesis with enhanced prosody consistency from facial video; improves reference prosody metrics and gets 54.22% listener preference, but not WER.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 54.22% ABX preference; WER 22.5% vs 22.1% baseline, unseen-speaker LRS3
limitations: No WER improvement; oracle audio cues and normalization changes complicate comparisons; limited perceptual study reporting; no runtime evaluation.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Brain-to-Speech Models Across Speech Modes
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Ayushi Mishra
summary: Applies activation interventions to a stereotactic EEG brain-to-speech decoder across vocalized, mimed and imagined speech; baseline PCC is 0.75/0.73/0.57, but internal inconsistencies leave strong causal conclusions unestablished.
task: Interpretability of speech reconstruction from sEEG
vocabulary: Paired sentences; lexical size not reported
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Baseline PCC 0.7519 vocalized, 0.7254 imagined, 0.5686 mimed (author-reported, unresolved)
limitations: One participant and one architecture; donor replacement bypasses recipient information, scores and winner counts are internally inconsistent, and no deployable imagined-only transfer is shown.

title: Multi-Subject Pretraining Enables Short-Calibration Personalization for Closed-Corpus Surface EMG Speech Decoding
authors: Chenqian Le; Beatrice Fumagalli; Yasamin Esmaeili; Xupeng Chen; Tianyu He; Nikasadat Emami; Adeen Flinker; Yao Wang
summary: Multi-subject pretraining plus target fine-tuning for 8-channel face/neck sEMG decoding of a closed 50-sentence corpus (27 subjects, LOSO); 21.7% CER / 31.9% WER, with 3-minute calibration not significantly worse.
speaker: Both
key_result: 21.7% CER / 31.9% WER, pretrain + fine-tune, closed 50 sentences; 78.6% CER on unseen sentences
limitations: Evaluation sentences can appear in other subjects' pretraining; performance collapses on unseen sentences; offline only, healthy adults, no latency or electrode re-donning tests.

title: NasoVoce: A Nose-Mounted Low-Audibility Speech Interface for Always-Available Speech Interaction
authors: Jun Rekimoto; Yu Nishimura; Bojian Yang
summary: NasoVoce, nose-pad microphone and vibration sensor on smart glasses, with multimodal fusion for low-audibility and whispered speech interaction under noise, evaluated by ASR error rates and audio quality.
sensor: Nose-pad MEMS microphone and vibration sensor in smart glasses
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: ASR evaluation uses synthetic noise; in-the-wild testing only qualitative; fusion not fully streaming; whispered vibration signals remain weak.

title: Physiological Noise Augmentation Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Speech
authors: Benjamin Ballyk; Teyun Kwon; Miran Özdogan; Oiwi Parker Jones
summary: Physiological noise augmentation (PNA) using ICA-derived artifact components for non-invasive MEG imagined-speech decoding; improves 10-class imagined digit accuracy, e.g. EEGNet 73.0% to 76.3% with 10-trial averaging.
sensor: MEG with EOG and ECG reference sensors
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: EEGNet accuracy 73.0% to 76.3% with PNA and 10-trial averaging, 10 classes
limitations: Single-subject MEG dataset only; requires recorded EOG/ECG reference channels; no unseen subjects, real-time or wearable tests.

title: Relating the Neural Representations of Vocalized, Mimed, and Imagined Speech
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Rupesh Chillale; Shihab A. Shamma
summary: Cross-mode analysis of speech reconstruction from sEEG in vocalized, mimed and imagined speech in one participant, showing envelope correlation needs sentence-discrimination checks.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Rank area above chance 0.59 (nonlinear, vocalized within-mode); cross-mode at most 0.14
limitations: Single participant; split, alignment and model-selection details incomplete; linear and nonlinear models use different targets and nulls; no online or intelligibility evaluation.

title: Silent Speech Interfaces in the Era of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Taxonomy and Systematic Review
authors: Kele Xu; Yifan Wang; Ming Feng; Qisheng Xu; Wuyang Chen; Yutao Dou; Cheng Yang; Huaimin Wang
summary: Taxonomy and review of silent speech interfaces in the LLM era across neural, EMG, magnetic, ultrasound, optical, acoustic and RF sensing, with benchmark and dataset tables.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: No reproducible review selection procedure; citation errors and mixed metric scales make its tables unsuitable for rankings or deployment claims.

title: SilentWear: an Ultra-Low Power Wearable System for EMG-based Silent Speech Recognition
authors: Giusy Spacone; Sebastian Frey; Giovanni Pollo; Alessio Burrello; Daniele Jahier Pagliari; Victor Kartsch; Andrea Cossettini; Luca Benini
summary: SilentWear, an ultra-low-power dry textile neckband with embedded CNN for EMG command recognition; silent balanced accuracy is 77.5% on pooled-day batches but drops to 59.3% on a new day.
sensor: Dry textile neckband, 14-channel differential surface EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 59.3% silent balanced accuracy on held-out days (77.5% pooled-day), 9 classes; 2.47 ms inference
limitations: Only four subjects and subject-specific models; large drop on new days; no closed-loop user study, walking or false-trigger evaluation.

title: SLD-L2S: Hierarchical Subspace Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Lip to Speech Synthesis
authors: Yifan Liang; Andong Li; Kang Yang; Guochen Yu; Fangkun Liu; Lingling Dai; Xiaodong Li; Chengshi Zheng
summary: SLD-L2S, a hierarchical subspace latent diffusion model for lip-to-speech synthesis that improves naturalness, while word accuracy and speaker similarity trail stronger baselines.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 30.22%, UTMOS 4.21; listener naturalness 4.17 vs 3.88 (V2SFlow)
limitations: Needs reference audio for speaker identity; WER worse than baselines; small listener study; no measured runtime or latency.

title: Soft Active Electromyography Interface for Machine Learning-Enabled Silent Speech Recognition
authors: Yuta Kurotaki; Shusuke Yamakoshi; Reitaro Yoshida; Yutaka Isoda; Tamami Takano; Yuji Isano; Yusuke Miyake; Kentaro Kuribayashi; Hiroki Ota
summary: Hand-worn soft fingertip dry-electrode EMG interface for silent recognition of 30 words with drone control; 97.2% mean participant-dependent accuracy across three participants.
sensor: Hand-worn fingertip dry electrodes, 4-channel facial surface EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 97.2% mean participant-dependent accuracy, 30 words, 3 participants; combined model 92.1%
limitations: Only three participants and a fixed 30-word vocabulary; no unseen users or words, repeat-session, latency, power or quantified real-world testing; recognition runs on a PC.

title: SoniSpeech: A Large-Scale Open-Vocabulary Tri-Modal Dataset for Wearable Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Ruidong Zhang; Jiacheng Liu; François Guimbretière; Cheng Zhang
summary: Single-speaker open-vocabulary dataset (ultrasound echoes, audio, video) from eyeglass-mounted sensors; an echo-only baseline trained on mixed voiced/silent data reaches 26.3% WER on silent speech.
sensor: Eyeglass-frame ultrasound speakers/microphones (FMCW echoes), audio, video
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 26.3% silent WER with mixed voiced/silent training (78.4% voiced-only training)
limitations: Single author in one quiet setting; population and everyday-environment generalization untested; baseline uses echoes only, not trimodal fusion; no latency or power measurements.

title: Speaking Without Sound: Multi-speaker Silent Speech Voicing with Facial Inputs Only
authors: Jaejun Lee; Yoori Oh; Kyogu Lee
summary: Multi-speaker silent speech voicing from one user's EMG with target voices conditioned on facial images, without inference audio; pitch flattening modestly improves silent WER.
sensor: Existing facial/neck surface EMG plus target face image
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Silent WER 38.91% with pitch flattening vs 40.12% without
limitations: Only one EMG participant; multi-user decoding and faithful personal-voice recovery not shown; main baseline is the same framework without flattening.

title: Toward Robust, Reproducible, and Widely Accessible Intracranial Language Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Comprehensive Review of Neural Mechanisms, Hardware, Algorithms, Evaluation, Clinical Pathways and Future Directions
authors: Dongyi He; Wai Ting Siok; Nizhuan Wang
summary: Review of intracranial language BCIs covering neural mechanisms, hardware, algorithms, evaluation and clinical pathways, proposing a composite weighted benchmark.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Composite benchmark is unvalidated with author-chosen weights; narrative rather than systematic; some source attributions and mechanism claims need correction.

title: Transfer Learning from ImageNet for MEG-Based Decoding of Imagined Speech
authors: Soufiane Jhilal; Stéphanie Martin; Anne-Lise Giraud
summary: Adapts ImageNet-pretrained vision models to MEG time-frequency images for closed-set imagined-speech classification, reaching 60.6% (pooled CV) and 51.7% (leave-one-subject-out) on three-vowel decoding (chance 33%).
task: Closed-set imagined speech condition and vowel classification
speaker: Both
key_result: Three-vowel balanced accuracy 60.6% pooled CV, 51.7% LOSO, chance 33%
limitations: Decodes task/vowel labels, not words or sentences; binary contrasts may reflect attention or residual sensorimotor activity; no online, clinical or communication evaluation.

title: Zero-Shot Imagined Speech Decoding via Imagined-to-Listened MEG Mapping
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Shihab Shamma
summary: Zero-shot imagined speech decoding by mapping imagined MEG to listened responses and decoding with a listened-trained contrastive model; above-chance word decoding with Recall@1 up to about 9.1%.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Recall@1 up to ~9.1% (combined embeddings), 76 words, leave-one-subject-out
limitations: Small 76-word vocabulary from rhythmic stimuli by trained musicians; low SNR; non-portable MEG; not tested on natural continuous imagined speech.

title: A Convolutional Framework for Mapping Imagined Auditory MEG into Listened Brain Responses
authors: Maryam Maghsoudi; Mohsen Rezaeizadeh; Shihab Shamma
summary: Maps imagined auditory MEG (melodies and poems) to listened-response MEG; 8-condition classification reaches 50.7% (chance 12.5%), and calibrated cross-subject CNN beats shuffled controls, but correlations are small.
task: Mapping imagined to listened auditory MEG
speaker: Both
key_result: 8-condition accuracy 50.7% (chance 12.5%); CNN mean r 0.0113 vs control 0.0063
limitations: Very small correlations, no speech or text reconstruction, 11 trained musicians in a shielded room, and incomplete implementation and split details.

title: A cross-species neural foundation model for end-to-end speech decoding
authors: Yizi Zhang; Linyang He; Chaofei Fan; Tingkai Liu; Han Yu; Trung Le; Jingyuan Li; Scott Linderman; Lea Duncker; Francis R Willett; Nima Mesgarani; Liam Paninski
summary: Introduces a cross-species self-supervised transformer encoder for Utah-array spiking data combined with audio-LLM end-to-end decoding, reporting state-of-the-art Brain-to-Text benchmark accuracy and imagined speech decoding.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER values not given in review; ~0.95 s end-to-end latency per sentence
limitations: Only two human participants; bidirectional attention and large LLMs hinder real-time, on-device use, and imagined vocabulary is limited.

title: A Parallel Ultra-Low Power Silent Speech Interface based on a Wearable, Fully-dry EMG Neckband
authors: Fiona Meier; Giusy Spacone; Sebastian Frey; Luca Benini; Andrea Cossettini
summary: A fully dry wearable EMG neckband with ultra-low-power BioGAP-Ultra classifies 8 silently articulated words for one healthy user at 68% accuracy, dropping to 54% on an unseen re-wearing session; acquisition plus BLE uses 22.2 mW.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Silent 68% (pooled 5-fold), 54% leave-one-session-out, chance 12.5%
limitations: Single participant, cue-aligned 1.4 s segments, no on-device inference reported, and no walking, natural conversation or patient testing.

title: A Silent Speech Decoding System from EEG and EMG with Heterogenous Electrode Configurations
authors: Masakazu Inoue; Motoshige Sato; Kenichi Tomeoka; Nathania Nah; Eri Hatakeyama; Kai Arulkumaran; Ilya Horiguchi; Shuntaro Sasai
summary: Jointly trains on EEG and EMG data with heterogeneous electrode configurations for silent Japanese 64-word classification, reaching 95.3% for eight healthy subjects and 54.5% for one patient (chance 1.6%).
sensor: Scalp EEG (63 ch) plus facial/throat EMG
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 64-word accuracy 95.3% healthy, 54.5% patient, chance 1.6%
limitations: Single patient, no EEG-only or EMG-only ablation, electrode and calibration burden, and no cross-day free conversation or clinical benefit shown.

title: An Introduction to Silent Paralinguistics
authors: Zhao Ren; Simon Pistrosch; Buket Coşkun; Kevin Scheck; Anton Batliner; Björn W. Schuller; Tanja Schultz
summary: Survey introducing silent paralinguistics: conveying emotion and speaking style, not only content, in silent speech, reviewing biosignal sensing modalities and open research problems without new experiments.
sensor: Survey of EEG, EMG, EMA, video, ultrasound, others
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Narrative review with no reproducible literature search, quantitative synthesis or new evaluation; silent prosody lacks ground truth.

title: Articulatory Feature Prediction from Surface EMG during Speech Production
authors: Jihwan Lee; Kevin Huang; Kleanthis Avramidis; Simon Pistrosch; Monica Gonzalez-Machorro; Yoonjeong Lee; Björn Schuller; Louis Goldstein; Shrikanth Narayanan
summary: Predicts 12-dim articulatory features, pitch and loudness from vocalized-speech sEMG and resynthesizes audio with an articulatory synthesizer. Feature correlation is about 0.9 against audio-derived proxy targets, but WER is 15.5% versus 12.6% for the Gaddy baseline (one male speaker).
sensor: 8-electrode surface EMG on face, jaw and neck
task: Articulatory feature prediction and speech synthesis from EMG
vocabulary: Open vocabulary (vocalized continuous English speech; size not stated)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 15.5% (Whisper) vs 12.6% Gaddy baseline; 4 electrodes give 22.9%; one speaker, 99 test utterances
limitations: Single male speaker with vocalized speech only; articulatory targets are audio-derived proxies, not measured articulation; silent articulation, other speakers, re-wearing and real-time use untested.

title: CAT-Net: A Cross-Attention Tone Network for Cross-Subject EEG-EMG Fusion Tone Decoding
authors: Yifan Zhuang; Calvin Huang; Zepeng Yu; Yongjie Zou; Jiawei Ju
summary: CAT-Net fuses EEG and surface EMG with cross-attention to classify Mandarin lexical tones in silent articulation, reporting 85.10% leave-one-subject-out accuracy over 4 tones.
sensor: 64-channel NeuSen W EEG plus 5-site face/neck sEMG
speaker: Both
key_result: 85.10% leave-one-subject-out (silent, 4 classes); 88.08% 5-fold
limitations: Tone classification, not sentence recognition; 10 subjects, metric naming inconsistencies, and unclear split and channel-selection procedures.

title: Confidence-Based Self-Training for EMG-to-Speech: Leveraging Synthetic EMG for Robust Modeling
authors: Xiaodan Chen; Xiaoxue Gao; Mathias Quoy; Alexandre Pitti; Nancy F. Chen
summary: Uses confidence-filtered synthetic EMG generated from speech, mixed with real data, for EMG-to-speech; on real vocalized EMG from one speaker, WER falls from 23.30% to 21.87%.
sensor: Existing 8-electrode surface EMG plus synthetic EMG
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 21.87% vs 23.30% baseline, real single-speaker vocalized EMG
limitations: Real EMG from only one speaker, no silent articulation evaluated, and figure/text inconsistencies and unclear splits remain.

title: Conformer-based Ultrasound-to-Speech Conversion
authors: Ibrahim Ibrahimov; Zainkó Csaba; Gábor Gosztolya
summary: Compares Conformer-based models to a CNN for ultrasound tongue-to-speech conversion on four speakers; Conformer plus bi-LSTM gives a modest naturalness gain without improving objective spectral metrics.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: MUSHRA naturalness 32 vs 28 (CNN), p=0.037, held-out sentences
limitations: Four speakers with ten test sentences each, low absolute naturalness, no intelligibility test, and no real-time or truly silent operation.

title: Distinct Theta Synchrony across Speech Modes: Perceived, Spoken, Whispered, and Imagined
authors: Jung-Sun Lee; Ha-Na Jo; Eunyeong Ko
summary: Exploratory comparison of EEG theta-band functional connectivity across perceived, spoken, whispered and imagined speech in ten healthy subjects; no recognition performance is measured.
task: Functional connectivity analysis across speech modes
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: No decoding evaluation, statistical tests are unspecified, PLI formula is inconsistent, and muscle or auditory confounds are not separated.

title: EEG-to-Voice Decoding of Spoken and Imagined speech Using Non-Invasive EEG
authors: Hanbeot Park; Yunjeong Cho; Hunhee Kim
summary: Reconstructs cued overt and imagined speech audio and text from 130-channel wet EEG with subject-specific models; imagined-speech WER is 47.48% (2 s) and 43.46% (4 s) before language correction.
task: Speech synthesis and text from EEG
vocabulary: 10 closed classes per condition (words and sentences)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Imagined WER 47.48% at 2 s, 43.46% at 4 s, closed classes, before correction
limitations: Random splits include every class in training and test, imagined trials use overt audio as targets, and no unseen content, real-time use or clinical test is shown.

title: emg2speech: Synthesizing speech from electromyography using self-supervised speech models
authors: Harshavardhana T. Gowda; Daniel C. Comstock; Lee M. Miller
summary: emg2speech synthesizes speech from face and neck surface EMG via HuBERT units without the user's own recordings; silent speech from one ALS participant gives 50.82% human-transcribed WER.
sensor: actiCHamp Plus wired gel surface EMG (31 channels)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Human-transcribed WER 50.82% (ALS, silent), 62.55% (healthy), unseen sentences
limitations: One subject per synthesis condition, high WER, wired gel electrodes, and no cross-day, re-wearing or everyday-use evaluation.

title: From Silent Signals to Natural Language: A Dual-Stage Transformer-LLM Approach
authors: Nithyashree Sivasubramaniam
summary: Corrects transcripts of speech synthesized from silent EMG (Digital Voicing data) with a Transformer recognizer and GPT-2, reducing WER from 36% to 30% on about 100 utterances.
task: Text from EMG-synthesized speech with LM correction
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 36% to 30% (DeepSpeech vs Transformer+GPT-2), ~100 utterances
limitations: Small test set, missing training and split details, no significance tests, and no check that corrections preserve intended meaning.

title: IR-UWB Radar-Based Contactless Silent Speech Recognition with Attention-Enhanced Temporal Convolutional Networks
authors: Sunghwa Lee; Jaewon Yu
summary: Contactless IR-UWB radar in front of the lips with an attention-enhanced TCN classifies 50 English words for one user at 91.1% mean accuracy, versus 74.0% for a hand-crafted baseline.
sensor: Novelda IR-UWB radar near lips (5-10 cm)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 91.1% mean accuracy, 50 words, leave-one-session-out (baseline 74.0%)
limitations: Single participant, requires alignment before each utterance, no ablations or statistics, and no unseen users, words or free posture tested.

title: Landmark Guided Visual Feature Extractor for Visual Speech Recognition with Limited Resource
authors: Lei Yang; Junshan Jin; Mingyuan Zhang; Yi He; Bofan Chen; Shilin Wang
summary: Combines 20 lip landmarks with image features for visual word recognition; with one-third training data on LRW-ID, accuracy improves from 85.75% to 86.65%, at larger model size.
sensor: Existing broadcast video (lip images and landmarks)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 86.65% accuracy LRW-ID low-resource (1/3 data) vs DC-TCN 85.75%
limitations: Small gain with more parameters and FLOPs, no seeds or significance tests, and no silent articulation, free sentences or real-time evaluation.

title: Lightweight Diffusion-based Framework for Online Imagined Speech Decoding in Aphasia
authors: Eunyeong Ko; Soowon Kim; Ha-Na Jo
summary: Real-time diffusion-based EEG decoder for one person with aphasia classifying three imagined Korean words plus rest, reporting 65% top-1 and 70% top-2 accuracy over 20 online trials.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 65% top-1, 70% top-2 accuracy, 20 online trials, 4 classes
limitations: Single participant and 20 trials; per-class and overall values are inconsistent, and no baselines, statistics or cross-day stability are reported.

title: LipDiffuser: Lip-to-Speech Generation with Conditional Diffusion Models
authors: Julius Richter; Danilo de Oliveira; Tal Peer; Timo Gerkmann
summary: LipDiffuser generates speech from mouth video plus the target speaker's enrollment audio using a conditional diffusion model. On LRS3-CHiME3 at -10 dB it improves quality and speaker similarity, but WER is 38% versus 36% for the best baseline.
sensor: Existing video (88x88 grayscale mouth crop); no new sensor
vocabulary: Open vocabulary English continuous speech (size not stated)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 38%, NISQA 4.57, speaker similarity 0.63 on LRS3-CHiME3 at -10 dB (1321 test files)
limitations: Requires the speaker's enrollment audio; natural-sounding output does not guarantee correct content; real silent speech, camera pose/lighting and on-device use are untested.

title: LTA-L2S: Lexical Tone-Aware Lip-to-Speech Synthesis for Mandarin with Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning
authors: Kang Yang; Yifan Liang; Fangkun Liu; Zhenping Xie; Chengshi Zheng
summary: LTA-L2S synthesizes Mandarin speech from lip video using English pretraining and tone-aware generation, reducing character and tone errors versus baselines, but CER remains 61.2%.
vocabulary: Mandarin continuous speech; size not stated
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: CER 61.2%, TER 40.9% on CN-CVS unseen-speaker split
limitations: High character error rate, ASR-based evaluation, unclear speaker-embedding source, and no truly silent or real-time evaluation.

title: MultiDiffNet: A Multi-Objective Diffusion Framework for Generalizable Brain Decoding
authors: Mengchun Zhang; Kateryna Shapovalenko; Yucheng Shao; Eddie Guo; Parusha Pradhan
summary: MultiDiffNet applies multi-objective diffusion learning to EEG decoding; for 11-class imagined speech, unseen-subject accuracy is 12.12% versus 10.61% for EEGNet, a small gain requiring per-user calibration.
speaker: Both
key_result: Unseen-subject accuracy 12.12% vs EEGNet 10.61%, 11-class imagined speech
limitations: Near-chance accuracy, calibration still needed for new users, a no-diffusion variant scores higher, and split and calibration details are unclear.

title: NaturalL2S: End-to-End High-quality Multispeaker Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Differential Digital Signal Processing
authors: Yifan Liang; Fangkun Liu; Andong Li; Xiaodong Li; Chengshi Zheng
summary: NaturalL2S synthesizes speech from mouth video without a reference audio of the speaker, using differentiable DSP. It improves quality and naturalness, but WER is worse than the comparison (30.4% vs 27.7% on LRS3).
sensor: Existing video (88x88 grayscale mouth crop); no new sensor
vocabulary: Open vocabulary English continuous speech (size not stated)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 30.4% on LRS3 and 36.5% on LRS2 vs 27.7%/33.5% for Lip2Speech Unit
limitations: Lip motion does not uniquely determine phonemes, so content errors remain; relies on large pretrained video models; true silent speech, real-time conversation and mobile use are untested.

title: NeuroTTT: Bridging Pretraining-Downstream Task Misalignment in EEG Foundation Models via Test-Time Training
authors: Suli Wang; Yangshen Deng; Zhenghua Bao; Xinyu Zhan; Yiqun Duan
summary: NeuroTTT adds task-specific self-supervision and test-time training to EEG foundation models, raising within-subject 5-class imagined speech balanced accuracy for CBraMod to 58.98%.
vocabulary: 5 phrases (hello, help me, stop, thank you, yes)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Balanced accuracy 58.98% (CBraMod, TTT with Tent), within-subject, 5 classes
limitations: Within-subject only for imagined speech, needs labeled user data, and participant counts, splits and statistical tests are unclear.

title: Non-invasive electromyographic speech neuroprosthesis: a geometric perspective
authors: Harshavardhana T. Gowda; Lee M. Miller
summary: Decodes silently articulated sEMG into phoneme sequences and English text without alignment to recorded audio, using a geometric representation of multi-site muscle activity. One healthy participant: PER 48.47% and WER 73.53% on large vocabulary; WER 14% on a 67-word date task.
sensor: 31-electrode wet surface EMG on face, jaw, lips and neck
task: Silent speech to text (phonemes and words)
vocabulary: Large vocabulary (over 6500 words); also 67-word closed set and NATO code words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: PER 48.47%, WER 73.53%, held-out sentences, one participant; WER 14% on 67-word closed set
limitations: Main result from one healthy participant with 31 gel electrodes, a stationary amplifier and manual segmentation; word decoding depends on a language model; streaming and day-to-day stability are untested.

title: Poster: Recognizing Hidden-in-the-Ear Private Key for Reliable Silent Speech Interface Using Multi-Task Learning
authors: Xuefu Dong; Liqiang Xu; Lixing He; Zengyi Han; Ken Christofferson; Yifei Chen; Akihito Taya; Yuuki Nishiyama; Kaoru Sezaki
summary: HEar-ID jointly recognizes whispered ear-canal letter spelling and user identity from in-ear audio and ultrasonic reflections; Top-1 word accuracy is 67.3% across 11 users (90.25% for eight selected users).
sensor: Modified ANC earbud in-ear microphone (whisper + ultrasound)
task: Spelling-based text entry and user authentication
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 67.3% Top-1 word accuracy across 11 users; authentication TPR 81.76%, FPR 3.2%
limitations: Depends on whisper, three users fail badly, hardware is modified, and no replay/injection attacks or unseen-impostor tests are evaluated.

title: Pretraining Large Brain Language Model for Active BCI: Silent Speech
authors: Jinzhao Zhou; Zehong Cao; Yiqun Duan; Connor Barkley; Daniel Leong; Xiaowei Jiang; Quoc-Toan Nguyen; Ziyi Zhao; Thomas Do; Yu-Cheng Chang; Sheng-Fu Liang; Chin-teng Lin
summary: Pretrains a brain language model on EEG with future-signal and frequency prediction, then classifies silently articulated words. Within-subject accuracy on held-out recording sessions reaches 39.6% for 24 words (TCNet 32.3%).
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 39.6% mean accuracy, 24-word classification, within-subject held-out sessions (47.0% for 6 semantic classes)
limitations: Only 12 healthy participants in a cue-driven seated lab setup with a dense EEG cap; no unseen-subject evaluation or confidence intervals; not tested online or for free conversation.

title: Reconstructing Unseen Sentences from Speech-related Biosignals for Open-vocabulary Neural Communication
authors: Deok-Seon Kim; Seo-Hyun Lee; Kang Yin; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: Reconstructs held-out English sentences from EEG and face/neck EMG with personalized models; overt EEG+EMG phoneme accuracy is 48.58% (EEG alone 36.83%) versus an 11% baseline.
sensor: 128-channel actiCAP EEG plus 10 face/neck EMG channels
vocabulary: 474 cued English sentences; 39 phonemes plus silence
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Overt phoneme accuracy 48.58% EEG+EMG, 36.83% EEG, held-out sentences, baseline 11%
limitations: Strongest evidence is overt/whispered, imagined results are from a representative subject, CER only for examples, and silent targets use overt audio.

title: RESOUND: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Videos via Acoustic-Semantic Decomposed Modeling
authors: Long-Khanh Pham; Thanh V. T. Tran; Minh-Tan Pham; Van Nguyen
summary: RESOUND synthesizes speech from silent video plus a 0.5 s reference audio by separating content and prosody paths; naturalness improves, but LRS2 WER (28.55%) is worse than LipVoicer (17.04%).
vocabulary: English continuous speech; LRS3 over 50,000 words
speaker: Not stated
limitations: Needs reference audio from ground truth, higher WER than baseline on LRS2, no variance or significance tests, and no truly silent speech evaluated.

title: Silent Speech Sentence Recognition with Six-Axis Accelerometers using Conformer and CTC Algorithm
authors: Yudong Xie; Zhifeng Han; Qinfan Xiao; Liwei Liang; Lu-Qi Tao; Tian-Ling Ren
summary: Uses six wearable 6-axis IMUs (accelerometer plus gyroscope) on the face and neck with a Conformer-CTC model to recognize silently articulated words and word sequences. Reports 97.17% word-level accuracy in a 4-participant study.
sensor: Six 6-axis MEMS IMUs on face and neck
vocabulary: 16 English words, 2 English sentences, 8 Mandarin phrases
speaker: Both
key_result: 97.17% word-level accuracy (correct words / total words), 4 participants; not sentence-level accuracy
limitations: Only 4 participants and a small closed vocabulary; accuracy drops for unseen users and some stay below 90% after few-shot calibration; real-time use, other days and re-wearing are untested.

title: Subject-Independent Imagined Speech Detection via Cross-Subject Generalization and Calibration
authors: Byung-Kwan Ko; Soowon Kim; Seo-Hyun Lee
summary: Detects imagined-speech versus rest states from 500 ms EEG windows in six subjects; accuracy rises from 67.0% (no subject data) to 78.1% with 10% subject calibration.
sensor: Scalp EEG (device and channels not stated)
vocabulary: 2 classes (speech state vs rest); no words
speaker: Both
key_result: 78.1% accuracy with 10% self-calibration vs 67.0% strict LOSO, binary
limitations: Detects speech state, not words; six subjects, unclear splits and statistics, and no real-time, continuous or patient evaluation.

title: Toward Practical BCI: A Real-time Wireless Imagined Speech EEG Decoding System
authors: Ji-Ha Park; Heon-Gyu Kwak; Gi-Hwan Shin; Yoo-In Jeon; Sun-Min Park; Ji-Yeon Hwang; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: Implements a wired and wireless EEG prototype classifying four imagined commands with per-user calibration; accuracy is 62.00% wired and 46.67% wireless (chance 25%) in three healthy subjects.
sensor: BrainAmp 32-ch wired EEG; Emotiv EPOC X wireless
vocabulary: 4 commands (help me, tell me, bored, tired)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 62.00% wired, 46.67% wireless accuracy, 4 classes, chance 25%
limitations: Only three subjects, unclear train/test splits, no rest-state false-trigger or identification results, and no mobile or patient testing.

title: Towards Unified Neural Decoding with Brain Functional Network Modeling
authors: Di Wu; Linghao Bu; Yifei Jia; Lu Cao; Siyuan Li; Siyu Chen; Yueqian Zhou; Sheng Fan; Wenjie Ren; Dengchang Wu; Kang Wang; Yue Zhang; Yuehui Ma; Jie Yang; Mohamad Sawan
summary: Shared training across intracranial sEEG with differing electrode layouts improves 23-class initial-sound classification for vocalized and silent (mouthed) Mandarin speech, but accuracy drops on unseen subjects.
speaker: Both
key_result: Shared training gains of 5.10% / 4.97% (silent offline, participants 10/11)
limitations: Only five silent and two online participants, random sample splits, reduced unseen-subject accuracy, and bedside setup with implanted electrodes.

title: Transfer Learning for Covert Speech Classification Using EEG Hilbert Envelope and Temporal Fine Structure
authors: Saravanakumar Duraisamy; Mateusz Dubiel; Maurice Rekrut; Luis A. Leiva
summary: Pretrains on overt-speech EEG and fine-tunes with the same person's covert (imagined) speech EEG to classify 5 commands. Reports 79.82% mean accuracy, though the simple mean of the per-participant table is about 79.07%.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 79.82% mean accuracy (reported), 5 commands, transfer learning vs 66.94% without transfer; 15 participants
limitations: Inconsistencies in reported averages; split independence and leakage controls are unclear; no control ruling out residual muscle artifacts; no online, unseen-user or daily-environment testing.

title: VSpeechLM: A Visual Speech Language Model for Visual Text-to-Speech Task
authors: Yuyue Wang; Xin Cheng; Yihan Wu; Xihua Wang; Jinchuan Tian; Ruihua Song
summary: VSpeechLM generates lip-synchronized speech from text, a reference voice and lip video by converting lip timing into phoneme sequences; WER is 12.5% on Chem and 18.3% on GRID.
sensor: Existing video; AV-HuBERT lip features (25 fps)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 12.5% (Chem), 18.3% (GRID) on generated speech
limitations: Requires input text and reference audio, so it does not read content from lips; table inconsistencies and no silent-speech use evaluated.

title: Wireless Silent Speech Interface Using Multi-Channel Textile EMG Sensors Integrated into Headphones
authors: Chenyu Tang; Josée Mallah; Dominika Kazieczko; Wentian Yi; Tharun Reddy Kandukuri; Edoardo Occhipinti; Bhaskar Mishra; Sunita Mehta; Luigi G. Occhipinti
summary: Integrates dry textile EMG electrodes into headphone earcups to classify 10 silently mouthed command words. Reports 96% accuracy on a random 80/20 sample-level split across 4 participants.
sensor: 4-channel dry textile EMG electrodes in headphone earcups
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 96% accuracy, 10 words, 4 participants, random sample-level 80/20 split (76.5% without filtering)
limitations: Only 4 participants with a sample-level random split; unseen users, other days, re-wearing, walking, latency and power consumption are untested.

title: Advancing NAM-to-Speech Conversion with Novel Methods and the MultiNAM Dataset
authors: Neil Shah; Shirish Karande; Vineet Gandhi
summary: Compares ways to create target speech for converting non-audible murmur (NAM) to speech and releases the 7.96-hour MultiNAM dataset. Diff-NAM gives final WER 32.39%/38.94% for two speakers, below Lipvoicer but behind MFA-TTS (26.38%/32.61%).
sensor: Bluetooth digital stethoscope behind the ear (NAM vibration)
vocabulary: Read sentences from LJSpeech (size not stated)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Final WER 32.39%/38.94% (two speakers) for Diff-NAM vs 26.38%/32.61% for MFA-TTS
limitations: Only two healthy speakers whispering prompted text; data splits and test isolation unclear; no listening test, no patients, re-wearing, noise or latency evaluation.

title: Adaptation of Tongue Ultrasound-Based Silent Speech Interfaces Using Spatial Transformer Networks
authors: László Tóth; Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; Gábor Gosztolya; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Uses spatial transformer networks to adapt ultrasound-to-speech SSI across sessions and speakers; STN plus output-layer update recovers most of the full-adaptation gain.
sensor: Micro ultrasound tongue probe with fixing headset
speaker: Both
key_result: STN+out: 88% avg cross-speaker and 92% cross-session error reduction vs full adaptation (MSE)
limitations: Only four speakers and MSE-based evaluation without intelligibility tests; still requires probe-mounted ultrasound and supervised adaptation data.

title: Audio Knowledge Empowered Visual Speech Recognition
authors: Jeong Hun Yeo; Minsu Kim; Jeongsoo Choi; Dae Hoe Kim; Yong Man Ro
summary: AKVSR improves visual speech recognition by transferring compressed linguistic knowledge from a pretrained audio model through a compact memory and cross-attention, without audio at inference. LRS3 WER drops from 46.1% to 41.6% (BASE).
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LRS3 WER 41.6% vs 46.1% baseline (BASE); LARGE reaches 23.6% with augmented data
limitations: Requires offline audio memory construction before training; benchmark-only evaluation without live, real-time or latency testing.

title: Audio-visual video-to-speech synthesis with synthesized input audio
authors: Triantafyllos Kefalas; Yannis Panagakis; Maja Pantic
summary: Adds synthesized audio from a first-stage video-to-audio model as an auxiliary input to a second-stage audiovisual video-to-speech model. Improves reconstruction quality and intelligibility on benchmarks, though gains vary by model and dataset.
speaker: Both
key_result: WER 2.65% on GRID (33 seen speakers); WER 24.96% on LRW unseen speakers
limitations: Depends on first-stage synthesized audio quality; WER gains inconsistent; no in-the-wild, noisy or real-time evaluation.

title: High-Quality Automatic Voice Over with Accurate Alignment: Supervision through Self-Supervised Discrete Speech Units
authors: Junchen Lu; Berrak Sisman; Mingyang Zhang; Haizhou Li
summary: An automatic voice-over system that supervises alignment by predicting self-supervised discrete speech units from text and lip video, improving lip-sync and speech quality on a single-speaker dataset. Not an SSI paper.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 24.7%, LSE-C 6.81, LSE-D 7.56, MOS 3.98 on single-speaker Chem dataset
limitations: Validated only on one single-speaker dataset; requires text scripts and pretrained unit tokenizer and vocoder; no multi-speaker or in-the-wild testing.

title: Improving the Gap in Visual Speech Recognition Between Normal and Silent Speech Based on Metric Learning
summary: Viseme-level metric learning that aligns normal and silent speech representations to improve silent visual speech recognition, reaching baseline parity with much less silent data on AV Digits.
sensor: Lip video cropped via Dlib face landmarks
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 6.66% VER, 9.97% WER on silent speech, 10-phrase AV Digits
limitations: Limited to 10 fixed phrases on small datasets; no open-vocabulary, continuous speech, real-time, or in-the-wild evaluation.

title: Intelligible Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Speech Units
summary: Lip-to-speech synthesis using self-supervised speech units as a pseudo-text target plus a multi-input vocoder; substantially cuts WER without text labels and reports state-of-the-art results on LRS2/LRS3.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Evaluated only on LRS2/LRS3 test sets with a 15-rater MOS study; no robustness to pose, occlusion, or lighting, and no latency or on-device analysis.

title: IR-UWB Radar-Based Contactless Silent Speech Recognition of Vowels, Consonants, Words, and Phrases
summary: Proposes FERASEC feature extraction for contactless IR-UWB radar silent speech recognition of vowels, consonants, words and phrases. With the upper radar and DNN-HMM it reports 86.47% vowel and 81.59% consonant accuracy.
sensor: Two IR-UWB radars facing lips and below chin
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 86.47% vowels, 81.59% consonants, 88.95% words, 96.88% phrases (leave-one-out CV, upper radar)
limitations: Controlled lab study with prompted closed-set items and limited speaker diversity; sensitive to user alignment and tooth blockage; no open vocabulary or conversational speech tested.

title: Knowledge Distilled Ensemble Model for sEMG-based Silent Speech Interface
summary: Distills a ResNet ensemble into a lightweight model for spelling via the NATO phonetic alphabet from 3-channel facial sEMG on portable hardware. KDE-SSI reaches 85.9% accuracy on 26 classes with 0.12 ms inference per sample.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 85.9% accuracy, 26-class NATO alphabet, fixed 4:1:1 split; model 21.1 MB, 0.12 ms per sample
limitations: Only 5 young male subjects, speaker-dependent; adhesive electrodes with precise placement; no unseen-word or cross-session testing.

title: Large-scale unsupervised audio pre-training for video-to-speech synthesis
summary: Pretrains the decoder of a video-to-speech model on large audio-only corpora, improving reconstruction quality on GRID, TCD-TIMIT and LRW, though WER gains are not consistent.
speaker: Both
key_result: PESQ 1.26-2.07, STOI 0.49-0.72, WER 2.66%-42.38% across GRID, TCD-TIMIT, LRW splits
limitations: WER improvements not consistent; objective benchmark metrics only, with no human listening tests, latency or real-world robustness evaluation.

title: Let There Be Sound: Reconstructing High Quality Speech from Silent Videos
authors: Ji-Hoon Kim; Jaehun Kim; Joon Son Chung
summary: Reconstructs speech from silent lip video using self-supervised linguistic conditioning, variance predictors and flow-based refinement. On GRID it reports WER 17.07% and MOS close to vocoded speech.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 17.07%, CER 9.17% on GRID; MOS naturalness gap 0.28 vs vocoded speech
limitations: Evaluated mainly on constrained GRID and Lip2Wav subsets; multi-stage pipeline with no latency, streaming or real-world evaluation.

title: LipLearner: Customizable Silent Speech Interactions on Mobile Devices
authors: Zixiong Su; Shitao Fang; Jun Rekimoto
summary: LipLearner enables customizable few-shot silent speech commands on smartphones with on-device keyword spotting and incremental learning; reaches 98.8% five-shot accuracy on 30 commands in a live study.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 98.8% five-shot (81.7% one-shot) accuracy, 30 commands, mobile app; ~422 ms on-device latency
limitations: Modest vocabulary and study scale; confuses similar commands, requires visible lips, and incremental learning adds user burden.

title: LipVoicer: Generating Speech from Silent Videos Guided by Lip Reading
authors: Yochai Yemini; Aviv Shamsian; Lior Bracha; Sharon Gannot; Ethan Fetaya
summary: LipVoicer generates speech from silent video with a diffusion model guided at inference by text from a lip reader via an ASR classifier. On LRS3 it achieves WER 21.4%, versus 86.2% without ASR guidance.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 21.4% on LRS3 test (86.2% without ASR guidance)
limitations: Heavy stack of lip reader, ASR and diffusion with hundreds of inference steps, unsuitable for real-time use; quality depends on lip-reader accuracy.

title: RobustL2S: Speaker-Specific Lip-to-Speech Synthesis exploiting Self-Supervised Representations
authors: Neha Sahipjohn; Neil Shah; Vishal Tambrahalli; Vineet Gandhi
summary: RobustL2S maps lip self-supervised features to disentangled speech SSL embeddings before vocoding for speaker-specific lip-to-speech synthesis. Reports improved intelligibility, e.g. WER 29.03 on TCD-TIMIT-3S.
vocabulary: GRID 51 words; TCD-TIMIT 375 sentences per speaker; Lip2Wav over 5000 words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: STOI 0.596, ESTOI 0.452, WER 29.03 on TCD-TIMIT-3S
limitations: Speaker-dependent or seen-speaker evaluation only; limited prosody modeling; no real-time or on-device deployment.

title: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Tongue and Lip Articulation By Pseudo Target Generation and Domain Adversarial Training
authors: Ruichen Zheng; Yang Ai; Zhenhua Ling
summary: Reconstructs speech from silent tongue ultrasound and lip video using pseudo acoustic targets and domain adversarial training, improving silent-mode WER by about 15% and MOS by 0.34 over TaLNet on TaL.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging plus optical lip camera
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Silent mode: 43.1% WER, STOI 0.517, MOS 3.33 on TaL corpus
limitations: Evaluated only on TaL with some speakers excluded; silent mode lags vocalized; requires specialized ultrasound and video hardware with no real-time study.

title: Ultrasensitive Textile Strain Sensors Redefine Wearable Silent Speech Interfaces with High Machine Learning Efficiency
authors: Chenyu Tang; Muzi Xu; Wentian Yi; Zibo Zhang; Edoardo Occhipinti; Chaoqun Dong; Dafydd Ravenscroft; Sung-Min Jung; Shuo Gao; Jong Min Kim; Luigi G. Occhipinti
summary: Combines an ultrasensitive graphene textile strain sensor in a throat choker with a lightweight 1D residual CNN to classify silent words. Reports 95.25% accuracy on 20 words and 90% few-shot transfer with 30 samples per class.
sensor: Graphene-coated textile strain sensor in a throat choker
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 95.25% accuracy on 20 words (93% confusable words, 96% long words); 90% few-shot transfer
limitations: Only 3 participants and small closed vocabularies; isolated word classification only, with no continuous speech or sentence decoding; transfer tested on few samples.

title: WESPER: Zero-shot and Realtime Whisper to Normal Voice Conversion for Whisper-based Speech Interactions
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '23), April 23--28, 2023
authors: Jun Rekimoto
summary: WESPER converts whispered speech to normal voice zero-shot and in real time without per-user paired data; conversion cuts Google ASR WER on wTIMIT whispers from 44.70 to 26.68.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: WER 44.70 to 26.68 (CER 28.38 to 12.70) on wTIMIT whispers, Google ASR
limitations: Relies on whispered rather than truly silent speech and is evaluated on whisper datasets, not silent-speech benchmarks or broad public use.

title: Zero-shot personalized lip-to-speech synthesis with face image based voice control
authors: Zheng-Yan Sheng; Yang Ai; Zhen-Hua Ling
summary: Zero-shot personalized lip-to-speech synthesis that controls voice identity with face-image-based speaker embeddings, needing no enrollment speech; validated on GRID with 13 unseen speakers.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Tested only on GRID's constrained vocabulary; speech quality below natural speech, with no open-vocabulary, in-the-wild, or real-time evaluation.

title: FastLTS: Non-Autoregressive End-to-End Unconstrained Lip-to-Speech Synthesis
authors: Yongqi Wang; Zhou Zhao
summary: FastLTS is a non-autoregressive end-to-end lip-to-speech system that makes unconstrained synthesis substantially faster without obvious quality loss, evaluated on Lip2Wav and GRID.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Benchmark corpora only with three speakers per dataset slice; no in-the-wild user study or live camera-to-audio latency test.

title: Improved Processing of Ultrasound Tongue Videos by Combining ConvLSTM and 3D Convolutional Networks
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth
summary: Combines 3D CNNs and ConvLSTM to regress mel-spectrograms from ultrasound tongue video, modestly outperforming prior architectures in accuracy and efficiency on single-speaker Hungarian data.
sensor: Micro ultrasound tongue probe with headset, plus microphone
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: MSE ~0.276, mean R2 ~0.73 on mel-spectrogram regression
limitations: Single-speaker dataset with no perceptual intelligibility testing, cross-speaker evaluation, or real-time tests.

title: Lip-to-Speech Synthesis for Arbitrary Speakers in the Wild
authors: Sindhu B Hegde; K R Prajwal; Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay; Vinay P Namboodiri; C. V. Jawahar
summary: VAE-GAN lip-to-speech synthesis for arbitrary speakers in the wild; holds up on unconstrained LRW/LRS2, and multi-speaker pretraining with 5 h adaptation nearly matches a 20 h single-speaker model.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Struggles with severe or non-frontal head pose and lip-ambiguity; benchmark-only with a small human study and no latency or deployment test.

title: Movement Detection of Tongue and Related Body Parts Using IR-UWB Radar
authors: Sunghwa Lee; Younghoon Shin
summary: Uses IR-UWB radar aimed at the chin to detect hidden tongue movement states, achieving at least 90% accuracy for each of four participants on a binary task.
sensor: IR-UWB radar with sinuous antennas and dielectric lens
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: >=90% accuracy per participant, 2 tongue states, 4 participants
limitations: Only two states, four participants, manual trial boundaries, stationary lab setup; no continuous speech, unseen-user, or vocabulary-level tests.

title: Multi-modality Associative Bridging through Memory: Speech Sound Recollected from Face Video
authors: Minsu Kim; Joanna Hong; Se Jin Park; Yong Man Ro
summary: Memory-based cross-modal bridging recalls audio representations from face video, applied to word-level lip reading (LRW/LRW-1000) and speaker-dependent GRID speech reconstruction.
task: Lip reading and speech synthesis from video
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Speech reconstruction shown only on speaker-dependent GRID; best subjective scores need an added WaveNet vocoder; no live or uncontrolled conditions.

title: Sequence-to-Sequence Voice Reconstruction for Silent Speech in a Tonal Language
authors: Huiyan Li; Haohong Lin; You Wang; Hengyang Wang; Ming Zhang; Han Gao; Qing Ai; Zhiyuan Luo; Guang Li
summary: SSRNet reconstructs Mandarin speech from five-channel facial sEMG using duration-aware Seq2Seq and tonal multitask learning, cutting ASR CER from 46.62% to 21.99% over the baseline.
sensor: Five facial Ag/AgCl sEMG electrodes, 2000 Hz
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 21.99% objective ASR CER, 6.41% human-listener CER, six speakers
limitations: Speaker-dependent with six speakers and controlled read sentences; no cross-speaker, unseen-word, real-time, or mobile evaluation.

title: SilentSpeller: Towards mobile, hands-free, silent speech text entry using electropalatography
authors: Naoki Kimura; Tan Gemicioglu; Jonathan Womack; Yuhui Zhao; Richard Li; Abdelkareem Bedri; Zixiong Su; Alex Olwal; Jun Rekimoto; Thad Starner
summary: SilentSpeller enables silent spelling text entry with an in-mouth electropalatography retainer, reaching 37 wpm at 87% accuracy in live entry and comparable accuracy while walking.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Live entry 37 wpm at 87% accuracy (best 53 wpm, 91%); 92% word accuracy offline
limitations: Strongly user-dependent; requires an obtrusive custom-fitted in-mouth retainer; offline tuning used only two main participants.

title: SVTS: Scalable Video-to-Speech Synthesis
authors: Rodrigo Mira; Alexandros Haliassos; Stavros Petridis; Björn W. Schuller; Maja Pantic
summary: SVTS shows a simple spectrogram predictor with a pretrained vocoder outperforms prior complex video-to-speech models and scales to large datasets such as LRS3+VoxCeleb2.
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Depends on large curated aligned datasets; weaker on unseen speakers and unconstrained conditions; no LRS3 WER or user study.

title: Towards Neural Decoding of Imagined Speech based on Spoken Speech
authors: Seo-Hyun Lee; Young-Eun Lee; Soowon Kim; Byung-Kwan Ko; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: Transfers CSP+SVM models trained on spoken-speech EEG to imagined speech decoding; accuracy is slightly lower but not significantly different from direct training in a 5-class, 7-subject offline task.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 26.8% accuracy (transfer) vs 30.5% direct, 5 classes, 7 subjects, p=0.098
limitations: Small offline within-subject study with only 5 classes and 7 subjects; no online, cross-subject, or larger-vocabulary evaluation.

title: VCVTS: Multi-speaker Video-to-Speech synthesis via cross-modal knowledge transfer from voice conversion
authors: Disong Wang; Shan Yang; Dan Su; Xunying Liu; Dong Yu; Helen Meng
summary: VCVTS performs multi-speaker video-to-speech synthesis by transferring knowledge from voice conversion, with speaker control from reference speech, on GRID and LRW.
sensor: Silent lip video plus reference speech
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Large seen/unseen speaker gap and vocoder-dependent quality; offline benchmarks only, requires reference speech, not validated interactively.

title: VisageSynTalk: Unseen Speaker Video-to-Speech Synthesis via Speech-Visage Feature Selection
authors: Joanna Hong; Minsu Kim; Yong Man Ro
summary: VisageSynTalk disentangles speech content and visage (identity) features for video-to-speech synthesis, yielding robust results for unseen speakers on benchmarks.
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Offline benchmarks only with a small MOS study (20 GRID samples, 16 raters); needs clean aligned video, no robustness to pose or occlusion.

title: VisualTTS: TTS with Accurate Lip-Speech Synchronization for Automatic Voice Over
authors: Junchen Lu; Berrak Sisman; Rui Liu; Mingyang Zhang; Haizhou Li
summary: VisualTTS conditions TTS on silent lip video to improve lip-speech synchronization for automatic voice-over, evaluated on the scripted GRID corpus.
sensor: Mono video camera (lip region) plus text script
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LSE-C 5.87, LSE-D 8.45, MOS 4.17 on GRID test set
limitations: Restricted to scripted GRID data with paired text; no unseen speakers, spontaneous speech, or real-time tests; does not decode silent speech.

title: 3D Convolutional Neural Networks for Ultrasound-Based Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: László Tóth; Amin Honarmandi Shandiz
summary: Shows a compact (2+1)D 3D CNN outperforms 2D CNN and CNN+LSTM models for regressing 13 vocoder parameters from ultrasound tongue video, with lower complexity and training time.
sensor: Micro ultrasound system, 64-element convex transducer, 82 fps
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Single-speaker read-aloud data, MSE and R2 only, no pitch, no listening or intelligibility tests, and no silent articulation or real-time study.

title: Advances and Challenges in Deep Lip Reading
authors: Marzieh Oghbaie; Arian Sabaghi; Kooshan Hashemifard; Mohammad Akbari
summary: Survey of deep lip reading covering datasets, pipeline modules, challenges and evaluation metrics; contributes no new model or experiments.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Literature synthesis only, with no original experiments or deployment evaluation.

title: An Improved Model for Voicing Silent Speech
authors: David Gaddy; Dan Klein
summary: Improves open-vocabulary silent-speech voicing from facial EMG using learned convolutional features, a Transformer and auxiliary phoneme loss, cutting WER from 68.0% to 42.2% (automatic) and 32.3% (human) for one speaker.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 42.2% automatic WER, 32.3% human WER (from 68.0%), single speaker, open vocabulary
limitations: Single-speaker lab data only; no cross-session or cross-speaker evaluation, wearable or mobility tests; human evaluation used only 40 samples and two raters.

title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Age Estimation Using B-Mode Ultrasound Tongue Image
authors: Kele Xu; Tamas Gabor Csapo; Ming Feng
summary: Exploratory CNN regression of child age from tongue ultrasound images, reaching validation MSE 2.03 on UXTD versus 3.64 for a mean-age baseline.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Validation MSE 2.03 on UXTD (baseline 3.64); 4.87 on UPX (baseline 5.35)
limitations: Not an SSI system; small child-only datasets, validation-set error only, and no external dataset or deployment test.

title: EMA2S: An End-to-End Multimodal Articulatory-to-Speech System
authors: Yu-Wen Chen; Kuo-Hsuan Hung; Shang-Yi Chuang; Jonathan Sherman; Wen-Chin Huang; Xugang Lu; Yu Tsao
summary: End-to-end EMA-to-speech synthesis with multimodal joint loss and a neural vocoder, consistently improving objective and subjective quality over prior EMA-to-speech baselines.
sensor: EMA with nine sensors (lips, jaw, tongue)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Small dataset (three speakers, 354 utterances each), small listening test, no cross-speaker testing, and intrusive lab-grade EMA hardware.

title: Improving Neural Silent Speech Interface Models by Adversarial Training
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Adds adversarial (GAN) loss to MSE training of a 3D CNN for ultrasound-to-mel-spectrogram mapping, giving modest objective quality improvements on Hungarian and English single-speaker corpora.
sensor: Micro ultrasound probe under the chin (tongue)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Modest objective-only gains on single-speaker corpora with limited data; no listening tests, real-time operation or multi-speaker robustness.

title: Neural Speaker Embeddings for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Trains x-vector speaker embeddings from ultrasound tongue video, achieving under 1% speaker recognition error on unseen speakers, but adding them to multi-speaker ultrasound-to-speech synthesis gives only marginal gains.
sensor: Micro ultrasound system, mid-sagittal tongue images at 82 fps
speaker: Both
key_result: Under 1% speaker recognition error on unseen speakers; single-speaker synthesis MCD 3.12
limitations: Multi-speaker synthesis gains are marginal and evaluated speaker-dependently on the same 31 speakers; no robustness to session or probe shifts and no live deployment.

title: Silent Speech and Emotion Recognition from Vocal Tract Shape Dynamics in Real-Time MRI
authors: Laxmi Pandey; Ahmed Sabbir Arif
summary: Sentence-level speech recognition from real-time MRI of the vocal tract, plus emotion and gender articulation analysis; reaches 40.6% PER on USC-TIMIT with a language model, beating earlier rtMRI baselines.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 40.6% PER on USC-TIMIT unseen data with language model
limitations: rtMRI is a large, immobile lab instrument with no deployable path; evidence limited to offline decoding on USC-TIMIT.

title: Silent versus modal multi-speaker speech recognition from ultrasound and video
authors: Manuel Sam Ribeiro; Aciel Eshky; Korin Richmond; Steve Renals
summary: Speech recognition from ultrasound tongue imaging and lip video on TaL80 and TaL1; adaptation lowers multi-speaker silent WER from 77.79 to 69.84 versus 39.34 for modal speech, showing a large silent-mode gap.
speaker: Both
key_result: Silent WER 69.84 (TaL80, fMLLR+adaptation) vs modal 39.34; TaL1 speaker-dependent silent WER 37.94
limitations: Silent-speech WER remains far from usable; relies on careful probe placement, corpus-style recording and adaptation, with no live interface evaluation.

title: Speaker disentanglement in video-to-speech conversion
authors: Dan Oneata; Adriana Stan; Horia Cucu
summary: Disentangles speaker identity from visual content in multi-speaker video-to-speech synthesis on GRID, enabling voice control; on unseen speaker identity control the best model reaches about 38.9% WER with 11.9% EER.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video) plus speaker embedding
speaker: Both
key_result: About 38.9% WER, 11.9% EER (gradient reversal), unseen speaker identity control, GRID
limitations: Closed-vocabulary read GRID speech only; intelligibility-control trade-off worsens on unseen speakers and speaker identity or embedding is required at inference.

title: Speech Synthesis from Text and Ultrasound Tongue Image-based Articulatory Input
authors: Tamas Gabor Csapo; Laszlo Toth; Gabor Gosztolya; Alexandra Marko
summary: Limited-data TTS augmented with ultrasound tongue images; combined text plus ultrasound gives the lowest test MCD for all 8 speakers, while ultrasound-only input remains far worse.
sensor: Micro ultrasound system with probe-fixing headset
task: Speech synthesis from text plus ultrasound
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Test MCD 5.442 (text+ultrasound) vs 5.652 (text-only) vs 7.153 (ultrasound-only), speaker 03mn
limitations: Not a standalone SSI: best system still needs text input; speaker-dependent, limited data, sensitive to probe misalignment, and no listening tests.

title: Sub-word Level Lip Reading With Visual Attention
authors: K R Prajwal; Triantafyllos Afouras; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Camera-only lip reading with WordPiece sub-word units and a visual transformer pooling front-end; reaches 28.9% WER on LRS2 and 40.6% on LRS3 with public-data training (22.6%/30.7% with extended training).
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 22.6% WER on LRS2, 30.7% on LRS3 (extended training); 28.9%/40.6% public data only
limitations: Camera-only lip reading rather than articulatory SSI; offline benchmark results only, with no live silent dictation, latency, privacy or in-the-wild evaluation.

title: Voice Activity Detection for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces using Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; Laszlo Toth
summary: CNN speech-versus-silence detection from ultrasound tongue images on one speaker (TaL1), reaching 85.2% test accuracy; removing silence slightly improves downstream SSI reconstruction (MCD 3.05 vs 3.12).
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 85.2% test accuracy, F1 0.9, ROC AUC 0.859, single speaker
limitations: Single-speaker data with speech-derived labels; no cross-speaker validation, live test, or robustness to probe shift and new users.

title: A comparison of oscillatory characteristics in covert speech and speech perception
summary: EEG analysis comparing oscillatory activity in covert speech and speech perception in eight participants; finds stronger low-gamma for covert speech, stronger delta/theta for perception, and theta-gamma coupling.
vocabulary: Small fixed lexicon of 1-2 syllable words
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Eight-participant study with a small lexicon; no SSI decoder, user study or deployment, and visible participant variability.

title: An Overview of Deep-Learning-Based Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement and Separation
summary: Survey of deep-learning audio-visual speech enhancement and separation, mapping design choices and noting the lack of standardized audio-visual evaluation.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Not a primary SSI contribution; no new benchmark or unified re-evaluation, and lack of standardized evaluation limits performance comparisons.

title: Continuous Silent Speech Recognition using EEG
authors: Gautam Krishna; Co Tran; Mason Carnahan; Ahmed H Tewfik
summary: Decodes continuous sentences from 31-channel scalp EEG recorded during silent reading using CTC and a 4-gram language model; WER is very high (about 75-84%), showing feasibility only.
task: Continuous silent speech recognition from EEG
speaker: Both
key_result: WER ~74.9-84.2% across 12-72 sentence test sets; cross-subject WER 92.55%
limitations: Very small dataset (four subjects, 30 sentences), very high WER, poor cross-subject generalization, no real-time validation, full wet EEG cap required.

title: Digital Voicing of Silent Speech
summary: Synthesizes speech from silent facial EMG by transferring audio targets from vocalized recordings; human WER reaches 3.6% on closed vocabulary, while open-vocabulary WER drops from 95.1% to 74.8%.
sensor: Facial and throat surface EMG electrodes
vocabulary: Closed dates/times set; open vocabulary of 9828 words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 3.6% human WER closed vocabulary; 74.8% human WER open vocabulary
limitations: Speaker-dependent with substantial data collection; open-vocabulary WER remains high and all results come from the authors' own data setup.

title: End-to-end Silent Speech Recognition with Acoustic Sensing
summary: Silent speech recognition from lip movements using smartphone speaker and microphone active acoustic sensing; reaches 8.4% average WER domain-independent and 8.1% on unseen sentences within a 54-sentence corpus.
sensor: Smartphone speaker and microphone (active acoustic sensing)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 8.4% WER domain-independent, 8.1% unseen sentences, 2.6% domain-dependent; 54-sentence corpus
limitations: Small 54-sentence vocabulary on a research dataset; latency, always-on robustness, power cost and field behavior not established.

title: Silent Speech Interfaces for Speech Restoration: A Review
authors: Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez; Alejandro Gomez-Alanis; Juan M. Martin-Donas; Jose L. Perez-Cordoba; Angel M. Gomez
summary: Review of SSI modalities for speech restoration, focusing on deployment bottlenecks such as latency, scarce patient data and modality trade-offs; cites ideal latency of about 50 ms, acceptable up to 100 ms.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: A review that synthesizes uneven prior results without a unified benchmark and does not itself resolve deployment obstacles.

title: Speech Prediction in Silent Videos using Variational Autoencoders
authors: Ravindra Yadav; Ashish Sardana; Vinay P Namboodiri; Rajesh M Hegde
summary: Variational autoencoder model for speech synthesis from silent lip video that models one-to-many ambiguity; on GRID reports STOI 0.724, ESTOI 0.540 and PESQ 1.932, leading Lip2Wav on ESTOI and PESQ.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: STOI 0.724, ESTOI 0.540, PESQ 1.932 on GRID
limitations: Limited to the GRID benchmark with Griffin-Lim waveform recovery; no speaker-independent, open-world or real-time evaluation.

title: Ultra2Speech -- A Deep Learning Framework for Formant Frequency Estimation and Tracking from Ultrasound Tongue Images
authors: Pramit Saha; Yadong Liu; Bryan Gick; Sidney Fels
summary: Estimates and tracks formant frequencies from ultrasound tongue image sequences for speech synthesis; best U2F configuration reaches mean R2 99.96 on joint f1-f2 prediction versus 90.01 for a Conv-BiLSTM baseline.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Mean R2 99.96 on joint f1-f2 prediction vs 90.01 baseline
limitations: Focuses on formant tracking and vowel trajectories rather than full speech reconstruction; single collected dataset, no cross-speaker or real-time device evaluation.

title: Vocoder-Based Speech Synthesis from Silent Videos
authors: Daniel Michelsanti; Olga Slizovskaia; Gloria Haro; Emilia Gomez; Zheng-Hua Tan; Jesper Jensen
summary: Predicts full vocoder features from silent face video with joint visual speech recognition training on GRID; speaker-dependent model reaches PESQ 1.90 and WER 15.1%, but speaker-independent performance drops sharply.
speaker: Both
key_result: Speaker-dependent PESQ 1.90, ESTOI 0.455, WER 15.1%; speaker-independent WER 51.6%
limitations: GRID-only closed-vocabulary evaluation with frontal video; speaker-independent results degrade sharply and no noisy or in-the-wild testing.

title: A Novel Task-Oriented Text Corpus in Silent Speech Recognition and its Natural Language Generation Construction Method
authors: Dong Cao; Dongdong Zhang; HaiBo Chen
summary: Proposes a task-oriented text corpus and a hybrid natural language generation method for building EEG silent speech recognition datasets; claims gains over template and neural NLG but gives no numeric benchmark.
task: Corpus construction for EEG silent speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Does not solve EEG decoding, relies on a narrow domain, and quantitative evidence is too weak to audit the comparative claims.

title: Autoencoder-Based Articulatory-to-Acoustic Mapping for Ultrasound Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Gábor Gosztolya; MTA-SZTE Research Group on Artificial Intelligence; University of Szeged; Hungary; Gábor Infusz; ginfusz@inf.u-szeged.hu; Ádám Pintér; Institute of Informatics; University of Szeged; Szeged; Hungary; László Tóth; Institute of Informatics; University of Szeged; Szeged; Hungary; Alexandra Markó; Department of Phonetics; Eötvös Loránd University; MTA-ELTE Lendület Lingual Articulation Research Group; Budapest; Hungary; Gábor Csapó; Department of Telecommunications and Media Informatics; Budapest University of Technology and Economics; MTA-ELTE Lendület Lingual Articulation Research Group; Budapest; Hungary
summary: Compresses ultrasound tongue images with an autoencoder bottleneck before predicting spectral parameters, giving more accurate prediction and more natural speech with smaller models on a single speaker.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging (2-4 MHz convex probe, 82 fps)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Improved NMSE, Pearson correlation and MUSHRA naturalness (exact values not stated)
