limitations: Single-speaker corpus only, no cross-speaker or cross-session testing, and no real-time or mobile deployment.

title: Brain2Char: A Deep Architecture for Decoding Text from Brain Recordings
authors: Pengfei Sun; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Edward F. Chang
summary: Brain2Char decodes text at character level from invasive ECoG with neural sequence models, reaching 7.0-10.6% WER for three participants on 1200-1900 word vocabularies; silent speech WER is about 40% and 67%.
sensor: Implanted ECoG grids (16x16, 16x8) on speech cortex
task: Sentence-level text decoding from brain signals
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 7.0-10.6% for three participants, 1200-1900 word vocabularies; silent speech WER ~40% and 67%
limitations: Invasive implant, per-subject and per-session calibration, only four participants, silent speech tested on two subjects with about 20 sentences, no cross-subject transfer.

title: Denoising convolutional autoencoder based B-mode ultrasound tongue image feature extraction
authors: Bo Li; Kele Xu; Dawei Feng; Haibo Mi; Huaimin Wang; Jian Zhu
summary: Uses a denoising convolutional autoencoder to extract ultrasound tongue image features, improving silent speech recognition over prior feature extraction methods on the 2010 Silent Speech Challenge data.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging (4-8 MHz microconvex probe)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 6.17% with DCAE features, single-speaker Silent Speech Challenge data
limitations: Single-speaker dataset only, no cross-corpus validation, and robustness to different ultrasound systems and head movement is not validated.

title: Lipper: Synthesizing Thy Speech using Multi-View Lipreading
authors: Yaman Kumar; Rohit Jain; Khwaja Mohd. Salik; Rajiv Ratn Shah; Yifang Yin; Roger Zimmermann
summary: Lipper reconstructs speech from multi-view lip video on OuluVS2 as a regression problem; the best three-view setting reaches PESQ 2.315 with 0.169 s end-to-end delay, though audio remains robotic.
task: Speech synthesis from multi-view lip video
vocabulary: OuluVS2 phrases, including OOV phrase tests
speaker: Both
key_result: PESQ 2.315 (0 deg+45 deg+60 deg views), 0.169 s delay; user study 80.25% audio-only accuracy
limitations: Robotic audio, lips alone cannot recover prosody, controlled OuluVS2 conditions only, and weak speaker-independent results.

title: SottoVoce: An Ultrasound Imaging-Based Silent Speech Interaction Using Deep Neural Networks
authors: Naoki Kimura; Michinari Kono; Jun Rekimoto
summary: SottoVoce reconstructs speech audio from under-jaw ultrasound images with two DNNs to control unmodified smart speakers; command success rose from 42.5% to 65.0% with the second network, versus 90.0% for real audio.
sensor: 3.5 MHz convex ultrasound probe under the jaw
task: Speech synthesis from ultrasound for voice-assistant control
vocabulary: ~500 training commands; 4 Alexa commands in end-to-end test
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 65.0% smart speaker command success (4 commands x5, two networks) vs 90.0% ground-truth audio
limitations: Only two participants, speaker-dependent, tiny end-to-end command set, bulky non-wearable probe, 2.61 s latency, and unassessed ultrasound safety.

title: Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interface Built on a Continuous Vocoder
authors: Moham Salah Alradhi; Géza Németh; Gábor Gosztolya; Tamás Gábor Csapó; László Tóth; Alexandra Markó
summary: Adds CNN-based continuous F0 prediction to an ultrasound tongue-imaging SSI vocoder, lowering pitch RMSE versus a discontinuous F0 baseline, with a non-significant naturalness trend in MUSHRA tests on four Hungarian speakers.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: F0 RMSE ~30.6 Hz vs ~65.3 Hz baseline; V/UV accuracy ~78.8%
limitations: Small four-speaker Hungarian dataset, speaker-dependent training, no speaker-independent evaluation, and naturalness gains are not significant.

title: Video-Driven Speech Reconstruction using Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Konstantinos Vougioukas; Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Uses a GAN to generate speech audio directly from silent frontal face video on GRID; speaker-dependent WER is 26.6%, while unseen speakers degrade to 40.5% WER.
speaker: Both
key_result: Speaker-dependent WER 26.6%, STOI 0.518; unseen speakers WER 40.5%, PESQ 1.24
limitations: GRID-only evaluation, frontal faces only, audible artifacts and poor voice consistency for unseen speakers; in-the-wild use is future work.

title: Harnessing AI for Speech Reconstruction using Multi-view Silent Video Feed
authors: Yaman Kumar; Mayank Aggarwal; Pratham Nawal; Shin’ichi Satoh; Rajiv Ratn Shah; Roger Zimmermann
summary: Reconstructs speech audio from multi-view silent video on OuluVS2 with CNN-LSTM models, showing multi-view input improves PESQ over single view and that camera placement matters.
task: Speech synthesis from multi-view silent video
vocabulary: Limited OuluVS2 phrases, digits and TIMIT sentences
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Higher PESQ with multi-view than single-view input (exact values not stated)
limitations: Controlled OuluVS2 data only, requires multiple well-placed cameras, controlled lighting and speaker-dependent training; no unseen vocabulary or noisy tests.

title: Visual-Only Recognition of Normal, Whispered and Silent Speech
authors: Stavro Petridis; Jie Shen; Doruk Cetin; Maja Pantic
summary: Compares visual-only recognition of normal, whispered and silent speech, showing silent speech is a distinct regime: matched-condition silent accuracy is 62.2% (digits) and training on normal speech lowers it further.
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Silent speech 62.2% digits / 64.4% phrases (matched training); 59.7% / 61.2% when trained on normal speech
limitations: Closed vocabulary, laboratory recordings only, accuracy far from practical silent communication, and no live interface shown.

title: Improved Speech Reconstruction from Silent Video
authors: Ariel Ephrat; Tavi Halperin; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Reconstructs speech from silent full-face video plus optical flow with a CNN and temporal post-processing network, outperforming prior methods on GRID and TCD-TIMIT in objective metrics and human word accuracy.
vocabulary: 51-word GRID grammar plus unseen words in TCD-TIMIT
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: GRID S3 STOI 0.68, PESQ 1.974; human word accuracy 55.8% vs 50.9% (Vid2Speech)
limitations: Per-speaker training, unconstrained vocabulary only partly intelligible, limited audio quality, and no real-time, unseen-speaker or in-the-wild evaluation.

title: Lip2AudSpec: Speech reconstruction from silent lip movements video
authors: Hassan Akbari; Himani Arora; Liangliang Cao; Nima Mesgarani
summary: Lip2AudSpec reconstructs speech from silent lip video using an auditory-spectrogram autoencoder bottleneck as target, improving objective intelligibility metrics and human word accuracy (55.8% vs 50.9%) over a baseline on four GRID speakers.
task: Speech synthesis from silent lip video
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Human word accuracy 55.8% vs 50.9% baseline; STMI 0.80 vs 0.52, four GRID speakers
limitations: Only four GRID speakers and closed vocabulary; lip-only input misses tongue and throat cues; no real-world recordings.

title: Seeing Through Noise: Visually Driven Speaker Separation and Enhancement
authors: Aviv Gabbay; Ariel Ephrat; Tavi Halperin; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Uses visual speech predictions from face video to build masks that separate or enhance a target speaker from audio mixtures, beating audio-only separation on GRID and TCD-TIMIT. Not an SSI paper.
sensor: Camera plus microphone (face video and audio)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: GRID separation SDR 5.62, PESQ 2.6 vs audio-only 1.74, 1.85
limitations: Not SSI; speaker-dependent models, unknown speakers need fine-tuning, and evaluation uses synthetic two-speaker mixtures.

title: Updating the silent speech challenge benchmark with deep learning
authors: Yan Ji; Licheng Liu; Hongcui Wang; Zhilei Liu; Zhibin Niu; Bruce Denby
summary: Updates the Silent Speech Challenge ultrasound-plus-lip benchmark with Kaldi DNN-HMM recognition, cutting WER from 17.4% to 6.45% on the same single-speaker archive.
sensor: Under-chin ultrasound transducer plus lip camera
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 6.45% WER (DNN-HMM, task-specific LM) vs 17.4% original benchmark
limitations: Small single-speaker controlled archive; no speaker independence, real-world robustness or live deployment evidence.

title: Vid2speech: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Video
authors: Ariel Ephrat; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Vid2speech reconstructs intelligible speech from silent face video on GRID with speaker-specific models and LPC-style resynthesis, reaching about 80% human intelligibility and partial out-of-vocabulary recovery.
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 82.6% audio-only intelligibility (S4) vs 40.0% prior work; OOV 51.6% vs 10% chance
limitations: Speaker-specific training, constrained GRID grammar, unnatural-sounding resynthesis, and a small listening study without open-vocabulary or live testing.

title: Contour-based 3d tongue motion visualization using ultrasound image sequences
authors: Kele Xu; Yin Yang; Clemence Leboullenger; Pierre Roussel; Bruce Denby
summary: Builds a contour-based pipeline that maps midsagittal ultrasound tongue contours to 3D tongue motion using a database of 1000 3D shapes; evaluation is qualitative, with about 1.2 s per frame association.
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported (about 1.2 s average to associate a frame with the 3D model)
limitations: Not a recognizer; uses only midsagittal information with a simplified driving scheme and has no quantitative accuracy benchmark.
